newsitem.title: USA: Simpson jury is read vital testimony in case.
newsitem.headline: Simpson jury is read vital testimony in case.

text.p: The O.J. Simpson civil case jury on Tuesday began hearing a reading of vital trial testimony to help them in their deliberations.

The first testimony to be read to the panel was that of Allan Park, the limousine driver who said he arrived at Simpson's mansion at 10:22 p.m. on the night Simpson's ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, were murdered, but got no response from the former football star until about 10:55.

Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994 murders by a criminal court jury in 1995. He is currently battling a wrongful death civil suit brought by the families of the victims and if the jury finds him responsible for the murders he could be forced to pay millions of dollars in damages.

Plaintiffs' attorneys in the civil trial claim Simpson committed the murders at about 10:40 p.m. outside his ex-wife's condominium, giving him plenty of time to drive to his home two miles (3 km) away -- a trip that takes four to six minutes -- and be there at 10:55 p.m. when Park saw him.

In the criminal case, testimony from Park, who took Simpson to the airport for an overnight trip to Chicago, was the only one the jury asked to be read to them and the panel reached its not-guilty verdict within minutes of hearing it.

As he did in the criminal trial, Park testified in the civil case that he did not see Simpson's white Ford Bronco parked outside his mansion the night of the murders, as Simpson claimed it was. In addition, he said there were no lights on in Simpson's house when he arrived and they were not switched on until he saw someone going in the door.
The civil case panel also was to hear a reading of Simpson's testimony on what he was doing the night of the murders -- in particular his account of his activities between 9:45 and 11 p.m.

The jury, after deliberating for about 14 hours over three days last week, was ordered to start from scratch on Friday by Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki after he dismissed the only black panellist for failing to disclose that her daughter worked in the Los Angeles County district attorney's office. The juror was replaced by an Asian-American man.

The reconstituted panel, which has debated for about 11 hours over two days, was also to hear Simpson's responses to questions posed by plaintiffs' attorney John Kelly, who represents the estate of Nicole Brown Simpson, about the Jan. 1, 1989, violent argument between Simpson and his then-wife, which left her bruised and battered.

On the witness stand, he said he never hit his wife on that occasion but took "full responsibility" for her injuries. The jury also was to have read back the testimony of Simpson's longtime friend, Al Cowlings, who said he took Nicole Brown Simpson to a hospital for treatment following the incident.
Finally, the jurors were to re-hear the tape of Simpson's interview with two detectives on the day after the murders.
The readings were expected to take up most of the day.
